title: Complaint under Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Suresh Yadav v. Singh Traders
content:
## IN THE COURT OF THE JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS, PATNA

**Complaint Case No. ___ of 2026**

**Suresh Yadav** ... Complainant

**versus**

**Singh Traders (Prop. Manoj Singh)** ... Accused

### Complaint under Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

**1. Parties.** The Complainant is engaged in trade of goods and supplied goods worth Rs. 4,80,000/- to the Accused.

**2. Transaction & Cheque.** In discharge of the said liability, the Accused issued Cheque No. 445210 dated 15-07-2026 drawn on [Bank Name], for Rs. 4,80,000/- in favour of the Complainant. [Section 138, NI Act]

**3. Dishonour.** The cheque was presented for encashment and was returned unpaid vide Bank Return Memo dated 22-07-2026 with the remark "Funds Insufficient". [Section 138, NI Act]

**4. Statutory Notice.** A demand notice was issued to the Accused on 25-07-2026 under proviso (b) to Section 138, calling upon the Accused to pay the cheque amount within 15 days of receipt. [Section 138, NI Act]

**5. Non-Payment.** The statutory 15-day period expired on 09-08-2026 without payment, and the cause of action for this complaint accordingly arose. [VERIFICATION REQUIRED: confirm date of service of notice on Accused to fix the exact cause-of-action date]

**6. Limitation.** This complaint is filed within one month of the cause of action, in compliance with Section 142(b), Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. [Section 142, NI Act]

**7. Prayer.** It is therefore prayed that this Hon'ble Court take cognizance of the offence under Section 138, NI Act, and proceed against the Accused in accordance with law.
